close_reason: Restated protect_last_admin rustdoc as an invariant-by-outcome contract: any apply_space_patch whose post-application projection has zero manage_members/manage_space holders MUST be rejected when protect_last_admin returns true. Enumerated the non-exhaustive op set (RemoveMember, UpdateMember role-strip, UpdateRole permission-strip, RemoveRole, and combinations). Also broadened the apply_space_patch error table at line 582 to match. Documented the reference MemoryBackend's intentional narrowness (RemoveMember-only projection per memory.rs:2838-2845) so readers aren't surprised. Commit cc85ca1. Verified by reading memory.rs which already documents 'production backends with stricter requirements can override apply_space_patch'.
description:
## Finding

\`ChatBackend::protect_last_admin\` at backend.rs:583-624 documents
the protection contract narrowly:

> Whether the backend should reject \`RemoveMember\` ops that would
> leave the target Space with zero members holding either
> \`manage_members\` or \`manage_space\` permission.

And later:

> The check fires inside [\`Self::apply_space_patch\`] atomically
> with the candidate \`RemoveMember\` mutation: the backend
> snapshots the Space's member/role state, projects the post-
> removal admin count, and rejects the whole update target with
> a \`forbidden\` SetError if zero admins would remain.

## What's missing

The protection contract is documented as **\`RemoveMember\`-only**.
But the same \"zero admins left\" failure mode is reachable via
\`UpdateMember\` that strips a role granting \`manage_members\` or
\`manage_space\` from the last admin. The doc says nothing about
this second path.

A third-party backend implementer who reads this doc and wires
the protection check only into the \`RemoveMember\` branch of
their \`apply_space_patch\` impl ships a backend where the last
admin can be silently downgraded — leaving the Space in an
unrecoverable state, exactly the failure the protection is
designed to prevent.

## Why this is a spec-correctness gap not a polish gap

Permissions in JMAP Chat are role-based (per draft-atwood-jmap-
chat-00). A user's effective permissions are the union of their
roles' permissions. The \"zero admins left\" invariant is invariant
on the *outcome* of any mutation that affects role/member graph —
not on the syntactic op type. The trait method's promise is to
protect that invariant, but its doc scopes it to one op.

The reference \`MemoryBackend\` impl may or may not extend the
check to \`UpdateMember\` (I did not verify). Either way the
contract gap stands: a third-party backend implementer cannot
reliably infer the broader semantics from the published rustdoc.

## Recommendation

Extend the doc at backend.rs:583-624 to enumerate the FULL set
of ops that can transition the Space toward zero-admin state:

- \`RemoveMember\` (the documented case)
- \`UpdateMember\` that strips a role granting \`manage_members\`
  or \`manage_space\` from a member who has no other such role
- \`UpdateRole\` that removes \`manage_members\` or \`manage_space\`
  permission from a role currently held by the last admin
- \`RemoveRole\` (or \`Destroy\` of a Role object) that drops a
  permission from the graph
- Any other op that mutates the (member, role, permission) triple

Or, more economically: state the invariant by *outcome* rather
than by op type. \"The backend MUST reject any \`apply_space_patch\`
that would result in zero members of the target Space holding
either \`manage_members\` or \`manage_space\` permission, computed
via the role-permission graph after the patch.\"

## Engineering basis

Direct read of backend.rs:583-624. The doc names \`RemoveMember\`
in two places (the one-line summary and the atomicity section)
and never mentions any other op path. \`UpdateMember\` is named
in the trait elsewhere (it's a real \`SpacePatchOp\` variant) so
the omission is asymmetric, not a categorical \"ops aren't
described.\"
title: API contract: protect_last_admin doc covers RemoveMember but is silent on UpdateMember role-strip path to zero-admin state
